name: Ruffhouse Records
ownershipStory: Started in 1989 by Chris Schwartz and the producer and engineer Joe 'The Butcher' Nicolo, out of Nicolo's Studio 4 in Philadelphia, with Columbia Records as distributor. Its first big success was Cypress Hill's 1991 debut, and it went on to release the Fugees and Lauryn Hill. Schwartz and Nicolo closed it in 1999, and Schwartz carried on with a new label, RuffNation. The Ruffhouse name was revived through EMI in 2012.
hook: A Philadelphia label run out of a recording studio, whose owners produced records themselves.
blurb: Ruffhouse began in 1989 inside Studio 4, Joe Nicolo's recording studio in Philadelphia, so the recording room and the company were the same place. Nicolo was an engineer and producer, so the label's owner was often in the room making the records. That is the basis of its one connection here, to The Goats, whose album Nicolo co-produced at Studio 4. Columbia, a much bigger company, distributed its records, the usual 1990s arrangement where an independent found the acts and a major paid to get them into shops. Ruffhouse released Cypress Hill's first album in 1991, The Goats in 1992, and later the Fugees and Lauryn Hill.
